rows.title: Maryland company promotes empanada tradition while giving Latin workers a job
rows.standfirst: Owner of this business says she’s on a mission to show the richness and diversity of Latin American food, one empanada at a time

rows.title: High Stakes: China and Mexico React to Trump's Re-Election
rows.standfirst: Donald Trump's return to the White House will reverberate through trade, security and immigration in China and Mexico. NPR's John Ruwitch and Eyder Peralta take us to both key nations.

rows.title: The story behind Cuba's economic dysfunction
rows.standfirst: This week, a powerful hurricane hit Cuba, causing nationwide electricity outages — right after a string of power failures that have plagued the country in recent months. These power outages are a low point for a country that has struggled economically for years and is experiencing mass emigration.

rows.title: How are world economies reacting to Trump's imminent return as U.S. president?
rows.standfirst: Economists and investors are expecting seismic and wide-ranging impacts from Donald Trump's second presidential term. A range of financial markets have already seen significant volatility this week.

rows.title: With the strike over, Boeing tries to refocus on what made the company iconic
rows.standfirst: Boeing's machinists are returning to work after a bruising strike. But the aerospace giant still has big long-term problems to solve if it's going to recapture its leading position in the industry.

rows.title: With Trump's win, Elon Musk stands to benefit
rows.standfirst: The billionaire businessman has spent weeks campaigning relentlessly for Donald Trump. That dedication could lead to major benefits for him and his companies.

rows.title: The Fed cuts interest rates -- but Trump's election could make things trickier
rows.standfirst: The Federal Reserve cut interest rates by a quarter percentage point. How much further rates fall could depend on how President-elect Trump approaches his second term.

rows.title: Canada orders TikTok's Canadian business to be dissolved but won't block app
rows.standfirst: Industry Minister François-Philippe Champagne said the decision to dissolve TikTok of its Canadian business is meant to address risks perceived to be related to TikTok's Chinese parent company.

rows.title: Amazon ordered to let workers vote on unionizing -- for the 3rd time
rows.standfirst: A federal administrative law judge says Amazon interfered in the last election on unionization at its warehouse in Bessemer, Ala.

rows.title: How personality trumped policy in this media election cycle
rows.standfirst: President-elect Trump has excelled at creating his own media image, from his earliest days as a real estate baron. His supporters find him entertaining and feisty, and even critics find it difficult not to talk about him.

rows.title: America's economy is the envy of the world. Will it stay that way?
rows.standfirst: Donald Trump's victory in this year's election had a lot to do with how many Americans feel about the US economy (surprise: not good). But Simon Rabinovitch, US Economics Editor for The Economist, argues that, despite the turmoil of the past few years, America's economy remains the envy of the world. Today on the show, Simon explains why that is, but also why he believes a Trump presidency puts America's 'economic exceptionalism' at risk.

rows.title: Moving to the American dream? (update)
rows.standfirst: Back in the 90s, the federal government ran a bold experiment, giving people vouchers to move out of high-poverty neighborhoods into low-poverty ones. They wanted to test if housing policy could be hope – whether an address change alone could improve jobs, earnings and education.

rows.title: Bernie Marcus, Home Depot co-founder who pledged to give away his billions, has died
rows.standfirst: A man of second acts, Marcus started Home Depot after getting fired from another retailer. He then became a philanthropist, a Republican megadonor and an evangelist of capitalism.

rows.title: Here's what Trump 2.0 means for the economy, from tariffs to mass deportations
rows.standfirst: Trump has promised to cut taxes and government regulations, slap tariffs on imports and order large deportations of immigrants. Here's how that could impact the economy.

rows.title: Here's how minimum wage and paid sick leave measures fared in the election
rows.standfirst: Some red states approved ballot measures to raise the minimum wage and require employers to provide paid sick time to their workers.

rows.title: Are debt collectors calling you about a zombie 2nd mortgage?
rows.standfirst: Old loans that homeowners thought were long dead have been rising from the grave as debt buyers move to collect. Some are allegedly breaking the law. If this is happening to you, tell us your story.

rows.title: Who's powering nuclear energy's comeback?
rows.standfirst: Nuclear energy hasn't been a growing industry in decades. But now, it seems to be making a comeback. This week, the Biden administration announced a goal to triple nuclear energy capacity in the US by 2050. And over the past few months, Amazon, Microsoft, and Google have all made deals to use nuclear energy to power their artificial intelligence appetites. Today on the show, could nuclear energy work differently this time?

rows.title: Fed up with high prices? Here's where things stand with inflation
rows.standfirst: Inflation remains substantially lower than it did during its 2022 peak — but Americans are still frustrated with high prices.

rows.title: 'Apprehensive and fearful': Federal workers await a dismantling under Trump
rows.standfirst: President-elect Donald Trump has vowed to "dismantle government bureaucracy," enlisting the help of billionaires to achieve his goals. Federal workers with memories of Trump's first term are scared.

rows.title: 'Jump ball' for Alex Jones' media empire as it hits the auction block today
rows.standfirst: Live bidding will be private, and the future owner of Jones' company will be public once court papers are filed. The proceeds will go to pay Sandy Hook families who won defamation cases against Jones.

rows.title: The strange way the world's fastest microchips are made
rows.standfirst: This is the story behind one of the most valuable — and perhaps, most improbable — technologies humanity has ever created. It's a breakthrough called extreme ultraviolet lithography, and it's how the most advanced microchips in the world are made. The kind of chips powering the latest AI models. The kind of chips that the U.S. is desperately trying to keep out of the hands of China.

rows.title: Why the government's flood insurance program is underwater
rows.standfirst: Major flooding events are increasingly common across the U.S., but homeowners looking for flood insurance will find few choices. The main providers of flood insurance is the U.S. government through the National Flood Insurance Program, or NFIP. But even though the NFIP is one of the only flood insurance games in town, it's drowning in debt. On today's episode, the NFIP's struggle to stay afloat.

rows.title: U.S. prohibits airlines from flying to Haiti after planes were shot by gangs
rows.standfirst: The shootings were part of a wave of violence that erupted as the country plagued by gang violence swore in its new prime minister after a politically tumultuous process.

rows.title: Dutch appeals court overturns landmark climate ruling against Shell
rows.standfirst: The original 2021 ruling ordered Shell to cut its carbon emissions by 45% by 2030 compared to 2019 levels. The appeals court said there is "insufficient consensus" on a specific reduction percentage.

rows.title: Why high prices toppled Democrats — and other governments around the world
rows.standfirst: Voters really don't like inflation. In fact, whenever there's a sustained jump in the cost of living, the party in power often pays a price.

rows.title: Why this former banking regulator is writing kids books
rows.standfirst: In a first-best world, we'd all save enough money and there'd be no scammers. In a second-best world, we'd all know how to protect ourselves.

rows.title: Israel's EL Al Airlines Turns Profits by Continuing to Fly
rows.standfirst: Israel's airlines are generating a windfall as international carriers cancel or limit flights due to security concerns. Flying in or out of Israel has become a logistical challenge since the war in Gaza erupted.

rows.title: A 'Wicked' mistake: Mattel apologizes for printing a porn site on its doll packaging
rows.standfirst: Mattel is pulling its Wicked dolls from some store shelves because of a misprint directing shoppers to a pornographic site. Meanwhile, resellers are listing the products on eBay for up to $500.

rows.title: What's a weather forecast worth?
rows.standfirst: The federal government has been tracking the weather for more than 150 years. Yet over the last few decades, the rise of the Internet and big tech have made weather forecasting a more crowded space. Today on the show: the value of an accurate forecast and the debate over who should control the data.

rows.title: What markets bet President Trump will do
rows.standfirst: On the day after the election, Wall Street responded in a dramatic way. Some stocks went way up, others went way down. By reading those signals — by breaking down what people were buying and what they were selling — you can learn a lot about where the economy might be headed. Or at least, where people are willing to bet the economy is headed.

rows.title: SEC Chair Gary Gensler, who took aim at crypto industry, to step down in January
rows.standfirst: Gensler said he would step down on Jan. 20, when Donald Trump will inaugurated as the next president. Gensler took big enforcement actions against the crypto industry.

rows.title: Bond vigilantes. Who they are, what they want, and how you'll know they're coming
rows.standfirst: As Wall Street investors divine what a second Trump administration might mean for markets, there's talk of a new gang in town: the bond vigilantes. On today's show, where they came from, what they want, and how to tell when they're about to spring into action.

rows.title: The Justice Department is trying to make Google sell off its Chrome browser
rows.standfirst: If a judge orders Google to sell Chrome, it could dramatically upend the multibillion-dollar online search business.

rows.title: U.S. charges Indian billionaire with defrauding investors, hiding bribery scheme
rows.standfirst: One of the world's richest people has been indicted on charges he duped investors in a massive solar energy project in India by concealing that it was being facilitated by an alleged bribery scheme.

rows.title: Veteran news editor expects Trump 'to go after the press in every conceivable way'
rows.standfirst: Former Washington Post executive editor Marty Baron says he thinks Trump is "salivating for the opportunity to prosecute and imprison journalists." New Yorker editor David Remnick agrees.

rows.title: The long view of economics and immigration (Two Indicators)
rows.standfirst: Mass deportations. What would actually happen—economically—if the President-elect follows through on promises to deport millions of people from America.

rows.title: The FDA says it found bacteria and a 'mold-like' substance at a Tom's of Maine plant
rows.standfirst: The agency is requiring Tom's to submit several documents, including assessments and remediation plans for its operations, contamination hazards, testing methods and more.

rows.title: How Magic Johnson's Starbucks created new neighborhood businesses
rows.standfirst: There's been a lot of research showing how third spaces — a place that isn't the home nor the workplace — have brought communities together, even catalyzed revolutions. New research shows that coffee shops in particular could be key to sparking new businesses, too.

rows.title: Traffic on Bluesky, an X competitor, is up 500% since the election. How will it handle the surge?
rows.standfirst: Unlike other social media sites, Bluesky allows users to create their own algorithm. The site does not have ads, nor harvest data for artificial intelligence training. But it is still very small, and it does not make money.

rows.title: Trump picks Wall Street investor Howard Lutnick as Commerce Secretary
rows.standfirst: President-elect Trump picked Lutnick, the CEO of investment bank Cantor Fitzgerald, to be his next Commerce Secretary.

rows.title: How to shop during a crisis
rows.standfirst: Events like the recent dock worker's strike and hurricanes sparked panic buying among American shoppers. Today, a logistics expert helps us craft a shopper's guide for how to navigate a supply chain crisis.

rows.title: Development of Elon Musk's rocket to Mars will likely take off under Trump
rows.standfirst: Regulators have slowed the pace of Starship launches over environmental concerns, but that may be about to change.

rows.title: America's first major immigration crackdown and the making and breaking of the West
rows.standfirst: Chinese immigrants sacrificed to create America's first transcontinental railroad. Its completion may have contributed to a backlash that led to the first major immigration clampdown in U.S. history.

rows.title: Defense pick Peter Hegseth paid accuser to protect his career, his lawyer confirms
rows.standfirst: The now-former Fox News host reached a settlement to resolve an accusation against him, but a recently released memo brought the issue back into the public eye.

rows.title: Spirit Airlines files for bankruptcy protection but plans to keep flying
rows.standfirst: Spirit Airlines says it will continue flying as it files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. Monday's announcement follows years of losses and a failed merger attempt for the low-cost carrier.

rows.title: SunFed cucumbers and Costco eggs recalled for potential salmonella contamination
rows.standfirst: Cucumbers shipped to the U.S. and Canada, and organic eggs sold in 25 Costco stores in five southern U.S. states, were recalled this week for potential salmonella contamination.

rows.title: Canada's Trudeau says he had an 'excellent conversation' with Trump after tariffs threat
rows.standfirst: The Canadian prime minister's meeting with Donald Trump at Mar-a-Lago came after the president-elect's threat to impose tariffs on two of America's leading trade partners raised alarms.

rows.title: O Christmas tree, O Christmas tree, which is more sustainable: real or plasticky?
rows.standfirst: It's time to discuss one of the perennial debates of the holiday season. Are real Christmas trees or their fake counterparts more eco-friendly?

rows.title: "Is it OK to ask about salary on the first date?" How to marry romance and finance
rows.standfirst: It's cuffing season: the time of year where the weather cools down and folks look for a warm body to cuddle up with. But we're getting into some of the less warm and fuzzy aspects of dating. For the next few weeks, we're kicking off cuffing season with some of the big questions about dating in our culture right now.

rows.title: China sentences veteran journalist on espionage charges
rows.standfirst: Longtime state media journalist Dong Yuyu met often with journalists and diplomats. His family believes he is now being persecuted for those exchanges.

rows.title: A social media ban in Australia for children under 16 is first in the world
rows.standfirst: A social media ban for children under 16 will be the first law in the world to levy fines on TikTok, Facebook, Snapchat, Reddit, X and Instagram for allowing youth accounts.

rows.title: Come for the roller coaster, stay for the shops: Can malls be fun again?
rows.standfirst: Mall of America's recipe for success includes an amusement park, pop-up stores, weddings and raves. Can local malls take a page from the country's largest shopping center?

rows.title: A TikTok sale under Trump? Experts say it could actually happen this time
rows.standfirst: Will TikTok be sold? The question has been asked before, during Trump's first term. But now, the situation has changed considerably.

rows.title: Federal judge dismisses defamation lawsuit against Fox News
rows.standfirst: A judge threw out a suit against Fox News by a former Trump supporter who said he got death threats when the network aired false conspiracy theories about his involvement in the Jan. 6 insurrection.

rows.title: How to watch Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, a tradition 100 years in the making
rows.standfirst: Macy's is promising its largest Thanksgiving Day parade yet, exactly 100 years after the tradition first started. Here's a look at what to expect and how to watch.

rows.title: More deals, more spending: What Black Friday has in store
rows.standfirst: This holiday shopping season is poised to break spending records. A new survey finds people plan to spend $771 on average.

rows.title: Why you bought your couch
rows.standfirst: You probably own a chair or a table or a sofa. And you probably think you know why you bought it. Because it was comfy. Or blue. Or the right price. But what if the style, the color, the cost, maybe even whether you would like it, were choices made for you years before you even thought about buying that piece of furniture.

rows.title: Trump's tariffs may be targeted at others -- but they could impact you too
rows.standfirst: President-elect Donald Trump threatened to slap hefty tariffs on China, Canada and Mexico. Those tariffs would hurt America too — if they are carried out.

rows.title: With a record number of international students in the U.S., Trump brings uncertainty
rows.standfirst: Some schools and international students in the U.S. worry about what's to come in the incoming Trump administration. Meanwhile, a new report finds more international students in the U.S. than ever.

rows.title: The price America paid for its first big immigration crackdown
rows.standfirst: The Chinese Exclusion Act was the first significant crackdown on immigration in American history. We explore the factors that led to the Act and examine what happened to the economy after it passed.
